memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked under HBM second-layer suppliers as a wafer-probing/probe-card exposure; survival to later layers depends on explicit HBM probe-card mix, memory customer concentration, pricing, and backlog evidence.
KLIC should be tracked under advanced-packaging bonding tools; thesis survives only if thermocompression or advanced-packaging orders become material enough to offset legacy wire-bond cyclicality.

MP is a reference leader rather than an underfollowed idea for rare-earth magnets; use it as the benchmark for policy support, valuation, and market attention when comparing smaller rare-earth or magnet suppliers.

NOPMF is an underfollowed rare-earth/magnet-material hypothesis; key uncertainty is whether it is genuinely an alternative to China-linked magnet supply or still materially dependent on Chinese-origin feedstock and operations.
FLR maps to nuclear EPC execution scarcity, not uranium or reactor technology; primary evidence needed is conversion of front-end nuclear work into full EPC awards with acceptable margins.

MIR maps to nuclear safety, monitoring, dosimetry, and compliance infrastructure; its relevance depends on Nuclear & Safety segment growth, backlog, services attachment, and plant-life-extension or SMR exposure.

ETN should remain the AI data-center electrical reference anchor; smaller electrical-service candidates need to show comparable data-center or hyperscaler-linked order evidence, not just broad electrification exposure.

IESC is an underfollowed AI data-center electrical execution candidate; key verification is backlog and margin exposure specifically tied to hyperscale AI data centers rather than generic commercial or industrial work.
MOS is not a direct copper or nickel hotspot beneficiary but can function as a sulphuric-acid scarcity read-through because phosphate fertilizer competes for sulphur/acid feedstock.
PRIM remains a lower-confidence candidate due to truncated input; track only if filings confirm utility, power delivery, substation, or transmission backlog tied to data-center load growth.

Company-specific relationships in this chunk mostly rely on candidate context and inference; Layer 2C should collect primary-source filings, earnings transcripts, backlog by segment, customer qualification evidence, and analyst-count/market-pricing checks.

Need pricing and attention checks for each ticker: market cap, one-year relative performance, valuation versus history, analyst coverage, short interest, and whether the chokepoint is already discounted.

Need falsification triggers by node: HBM tool demand slowdown, memory capex cuts, rare-earth export normalization, failed magnet qualification, nuclear project delays, data-center power capex deferral, acid/sulphur supply normalization, or margin compression from execution risk.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships across several hotspot chokepoints: HBM/advanced-packaging second-layer suppliers, rare-earth magnet supply, nuclear execution and safety infrastructure, AI data-center electrical balance-of-plant, and sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock stress. Reference leaders such as MP and ETN are retained as context anchors, while the main underfollowed lane centers on companies where the exposure is embedded in tools, qualification, services, materials logistics, or compliance rather than obvious headline demand. Evidence quality remains mixed: the strongest external support in this call is for HBM suppliers beneath producers, sulphur/acid disruption, and InP export-control context, while most company-specific relationships still require primary-source verification from filings, earnings transcripts, backlog disclosures, segment revenue, and customer qualification data.
